Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a problem by breaking it down into smaller, simpler versions of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a base case — a condition that stops the function from calling itself, preventing an infinite loop. Think of it like Russian nesting dolls: each doll contains a smaller version of itself, until you reach the smallest doll that can't open any further. With each recursive call, the problem gets closer to that base case, and then the results bubble back up to give you the final answer.
